derivation.method: remaining = targeted − completed per region, where completed = status ∈ {completed, completed-after-retry} and remaining = status ∈ {scheduled, failed-pending-retry, rolled-back}; stalled load = remaining in regions with zero completions in the trailing 28d window ending at the snapshot as-of date

current = completions (status ∈ {completed, completed-after-retry}) in the 28d window ending at the snapshot as-of date ÷ 4; required = remaining devices (status ∈ {scheduled, failed-pending-retry, rolled-back}) ÷ weeks from the as-of date to the close date
current and required rates recomputed with the 28d window anchored at the latest completed_date in the pin instead of the snapshot as-of date

on-site-remaining campaign devices (method = onsite, status ∈ {scheduled, failed-pending-retry, rolled-back} — i.e. not completed/completed-after-retry) joined to the fleet registry by device_serial; convertible = connected == yes

on-site-remaining devices (method = onsite, status ∈ {scheduled, failed-pending-retry, rolled-back}) × mean completed (status ∈ {completed, completed-after-retry}) on-site duration_min ÷ fse_day_minutes; labor time only — travel/overhead not in the campaign data (lower bound)

provenance.note: no corpus dataset acquired yet — roster, utilization, travel, and visits-per-day are needed for hire/contract/slip; the duration-basis floor is a bridge, not a substitute

verdicts.headline: Capacity gap to hit the 2026-09-30 close — APAC, EMEA, NA STALLED (zero completions in the four weeks to 2026-10-05; APAC needs 42.0/wk; EMEA needs 59.0/wk; NA needs 44.0/wk); remote conversion covers 0 of 97 on-site-remaining devices today

issues.statement: APAC wave is stalled under the uniform criterion — zero completions in the four weeks to 2026-10-05 (last completion 2026-07-18, 42 devices remaining, 42.0/wk now required)
issues.action: Re-engage site scheduling this week; re-baseline the wave or assign surge FSE capacity; confirm root cause (scheduling vs the failure cluster)

risks.statement: The remote-conversion recovery lever is sized at 0 of 97 on-site-remaining devices — the fleet connectivity join shows the on-site backlog is unconnected, so conversion first requires connectivity (adapters), it is not a scheduling change
risks.mitigation: Price the adapter retrofit against continued on-site visits (the BQ-30 upgrade-economics answer); otherwise the levers are contract labor or slip — noting the remote path carried the implicated failure mode (4 of 4 rollbacks were remote installs), so converted devices inherit that exposure until the failure cluster is resolved

risks.statement: The hire/contract/slip decision is being made on run-rate projections plus a labor-time-only workload floor (19.7 FSE-days) — FSE roster, utilization, travel, and visits-per-day are not yet a corpus dataset
risks.mitigation: Acquire an internal service-roster dataset; until then treat capacity conclusions as directional

watch.statement: Completion-rate trend by region (weekly, zero-filled) — a flatline is a stall, not missing data

expectations.statement: Existing field-service capacity absorbs the remaining waves without surge or slip
expectations.expected: current run-rate >= required rate through 2026-09-30 in every region
expectations.basis: implicit in the wave plan; never validated against an FSE roster (dataset gap)
expectations.actual: APAC: stalled (42.0/wk required); EMEA: stalled (59.0/wk required); NA: stalled (44.0/wk required)
